https://telex.hu/english/2026/08/12/hung.text: Menü Kereső Hungarian PM announces measures for raising Danube water levels at Hungary's only nuclear power plant English Nádor András Andrea Horváth Kávai (translation) Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom “We have ordered the immediate construction of a weir on the Danube and have also ordered that simultaneous preparations be made for a temporary solution,” Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar announced at an extraordinary press briefing on Wednesday. “Following today’s on-site inspection, and based on the unanimous recommendation of water management, energy, and defense experts, the government has decided to immediately-as early as tomorrow-begin the construction of a weir on the Danube between the river's two banks, specifically, between the Paks Nuclear Power Plant and Dunaszentbenedek, using 35,000 cubic meters of stone in the first phase, followed by an additional 110,000 cubic meters later." According to the Prime Minister, “within a few weeks”, the investment should ensure “that the water level of the Danube at the nuclear power plant’s cooling channel remains above minus 90 cm, allowing Hungary’s most important power plant to operate at full capacity.” He also announced the government’s decision to "simultaneously place two 80-meter-long barges on standby at Paks, which is necessary due to the anticipated rapid drop in water levels". “If needed, we will be ready to raise the Danube’s water level by up to 20 centimeters in the short term by the controlled sinking of these two barges, so that a complete shutdown of the Paks power plant can be avoided until the permanent weir is completed.” Magyar said that the construction of the weir and the readying of the barges will work in conjunction with one another. He believes this to be the most effective and safest solution at this time, and noted that it is supported by experts and authorities alike. The Prime Minister entrusted General Pál Kádár, head of the Defense Administration Office with coordinating the work. According to the PM, one of the barges needed for the temporary solution will arrive from Mohács as early as tonight, and the second one will be in Paks tomorrow. In light of the changing climate conditions, the Paks municipal council had previously submitted a proposal to the government, requesting that all possible solutions that would ensure the long-term, safe supply of cooling water for the Paks Nuclear Power Plant be considered. Speaking about the content of the petition, István Barnabás, Deputy Mayor of Paks, said that the local government is not proposing any specific technical solution, but is rather requesting an examination of all viable options and a resolution of the problems stemming from low water levels. Péter Magyar previously announced that the government would hold a meeting at the Paks Nuclear Power Plant on Wednesday. His Wednesday post revealed that, unlike the government ministers who traveled by bus, he flew to the meeting in a helicopter, as he explained, so that “before important government decisions are made, water management experts and the power plant’s managers could provide an overview of the current situation and outline the long-term solutions proposed by the engineers from above.” Magyar had announced on Monday that turbine 3 of unit 2 at Hungary's only nuclear power plant had been switched back on, which means that there are now two turbines generating power. This was possible because the Danube’s water level had risen 19 centimeters above the lowest level recorded more than a week ago. Based on current trends, however, the water level is expected to stagnate and remain extremely low following its recent drop; and as experts have warned, going forward, the frequency of droughts is expected to increase, with Hungary's rivers likely to carry very little water in the future. Telex previously spoke with experts of the field about the effects of the current, historic drought on Hungary's rivers and lakes, and the country's water and energy supply, as well as the potential solutions for the future . Notifications are sent through the electronic application for registration and management of the support measure financed from Swiss-Romanian funds. According to the procedural provisions of the aid scheme, within a maximum of 5 working days from the receipt of the notification of acceptance in principle to the financing, applicants have the obligation to go to the credit institution for which they have opted, in order to obtain the loan. In order to ensure compliance with this deadline and to reduce the risk of rejection for this reason, all applicants who have received letters of acceptance in principle for funding through the information system will be contacted individually by MEDAT’s technical staff, in order to be notified about this novelty and the next steps. We remind you that, on this date, the available budget allocated to the program continues to allow the registration and financing of new applicants, and the electronic submission stage of the registration forms is still open on the https://sme-ecotech.gov.ro platform. In this context, all companies interested in obtaining an investment grant in the maximum amount of 267,240 lei, approximately 50,800 euros, can register until September 24, 2026 for the support measure . The conditions of application, as well as the flexibility decisions adopted by MEDAT, offer all categories of enterprises, from all types of activities eligible for de minimis aid, the chance to participate in the program and benefit from non-reimbursable financial aid. The support measure is financed by the second non-reimbursable Swiss financial contribution granted to Romania through the Swiss-Romanian Cooperation Programme, aimed at reducing economic and social disparities within the European Union. Background information: SME Eco-Tech is implemented by MEDAT within the Swiss-Romanian Cooperation Programme. The objectives of the programme are to reduce the impact on the environment, increase the competitiveness and productivity of enterprises, stimulate domestic production and support employment. The total budget of the program for the period 2025–2027 is CHF 54,041,886, equivalent to 288,843,072 lei. This de minimis aid scheme is estimated to finance at least 800 SMEs in all eight development regions of Romania. Funding will be awarded in the order of submission of applications, according to the “first come, first served” principle. https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/27/serb.text: For the first time in nearly a decade, a Serbian media hosted a televised election debate with opposing politicians which drew significant public attention ahead of the 25 October parliamentary vote, in Serbia's highly polarised media and tense society landscape. Equally for the first time, a top official from the ruling Serbian Progressive Party appeared on N1 television in a live election debate.Ana Brnabic, Speaker of the outgoing parliament and a former prime minister, as well as top figure in Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic's political camp, faced the top candidate of the opposition Student List - Students win political platform and Dean of the Arts University in Belgrade, Mirjana Nikolic.The two contenders agreed to appear together live, but not without hesitations, and engaged in a fiery one-on-one debate, confronting their views on education, the chosen theme of the debate, before descending into the wider Serbian society turmoil and political conflict.The N1 televised debate was the most watched programme during its time slot, with a rating of over 48 points, and the most followed television show of the past month.The N1 host invited them to present their programmes, but the contenders went into trading accusations of violence, mismanagement and intolerance which matched the heated national political discourse as the country is gearing up for early elections called after months of demonstrations and protests which led to violent incidents.Triggered by the collapse of a concrete canopy at the Novi Sad railway station in November 2024 which killed 16 people, the protests were started by students who blocked state universities for a prolonged period of time before spreading across the country. The protesters blamed the tragedy on corruption and mismanagement. Eventually, the ad-hoc student movement registered their political list for the elections and are now seen by part of the public and by most pollsters as the main challengers to president Vucic’s rule.The political tension was obvious even before the TV debate started, with Brnabic declaring that Nikolic would not even shake her hand when they met in the studio.“You are constantly offending me, starting from your refusal to shake my hand. I consider that to be a basic human gesture. Generals are at war with each other and still shake hands,” Brnabic said.She asked her contender if “is that your decent Serbia?,” to which Nikolic fired back saying “decent Serbia is yet to come.”The intense buzz around the debateThe debate sparked surprise and stirred significant interest in Serbia as government officials have largely avoided the N1 channel throughout multiple election cycles, claiming negative bias, a qualification N1 rejected.At the same time, not many expected such a programme to happen at all as real debates by political opponents are rare in Serbia, with the media openly supporting one political camp or the other and thus rarely inviting politicians or activists across the partisan lines. In turn, politicians rarely agree to take part in programmes at channels they deem to be hostile and combative.Therefore, the debate surprised Serbia and, moreover, that it was hosted by N1 television whose editorial policy has so far been seen as consistently and openly anti-Vucic. Viewers have not seen government or ruling party officials on N1 since at least 2017.Ana Brnabic, who is in third position on Vucic's United Serbia electoral list, said she has not been on N1 since 2017, stating that “in previous election campaigns N1 would not even allow us to have paid promo clips (in their programme), that is how objective you were.""I wasn’t thrilled about coming now either, remembering how your television tried to dehumanise my friend and my president. You criminalised him. I could hear in your programme that he was the product of a viper’s nest,” Brnabic said.She then explained why she eventually accepted the N1 debate invitation, saying “I came because Aleksandar Vucic insisted. You changed your owner and the man said let’s give them a chance, let the people see how unbiased you are.”Brnabic referred to N1 television recently changing its ownership. Alpac Capital, a Portuguese private equity and venture capital investment firm, which also owns Euronews, acquired the ownership of the channel as part of a wider regional media acquisition. Alpac promised the media's business transformation and no direct influence on the editorial decisions other than the request for a professional, unbiased, objective and fair reporting.Viewers and politicians alike therefore watched the debate as a test and as one of many to come in the month leading to the elections as the channel said it would organise further thematic debates in the run-up to voting day.The representative of the opposition in the debate, Mirjana Nikolic, said she was also skeptical about the odds that the debate could happen when "the invitation came through regular channels, straight from the media."Nikolic said she wondered whether the debate was indeed an opportunity and "whether it was the right moment to take part in this debate," explaining that she did not know "whether their (the channel) concept would allow for the other side to come.""I was fearful because recently it became unpleasant to talk to someone who comes from the position of power," Nikolic went further, adding that "Ms. Brnabic has the advantage of having all the information at her disposal. Also, our recent meeting at the parliamentary committee for education was full of shouting, stomping and humiliating opponents, so there’s a danger in that.”Heated exchanges between the two contendersAfter a botched handshake attempt at the start of the debate, the contenders engaged in a series of heated exchanges, multiple accusations and both sides claiming they were offended. They sifted through the incidents of recent months, including the beaten students and the disruptions across Serbia.Brnabic criticised the students protests, the university blockades and the Students List political platform, while Nikolic argued that voters deserved to hear and the proposals of the other electoral lists for education and the country's youth.Ana Brnabic hailed the government's achievements on education, saying that the education budget has been increased more than threefold since 2012, from 140 billion dinars (over 1 billion Euros) to 425 billion (3.6 billion Euros). She added that the percentage of children going to pre-school increased from 48 to 64% and that four science and technology parks were built alongside investments in digitalisation.“Teacher’s salary went up from 391 euro in 2012 to 1,030 euro by December 2026. That is 2.6 times higher. University professors earned 77,000 dinars (655 Euros) in 2012 and by the end of this year they will earn 191,000 dinars (1,600 Euros). That is 2.5 times increase. This is what we did for their dignity and their living standard, to thank them for all they did,” said Brnabic.Nikolic countered that figures are not for television and that they can be misleading as it is uncertain that the teachers, despite the increases, can buy what they could in 2012.“We want dignity, professionalism and safety. In the complex of ideas we stand for, free education in the absolute frontrunner. We stand for free education, not as a populist phrase “free school books”, but for truly free education in all its aspects,” said Nikolic.She ended by telling Brnabic that she "failed the exam".The debate ignited Serbian social media, with many commenting its novelty, the nature of the debate and its takeaways as well as the performances and the punches by the two contenders, with both camps declaring victory. Some doubted it as an intermittent democratic exercise or its concrete conclusions, while others said that the N1 debate could now signal an improvement in Serbia's polarised media landscape and its culture of dialogue.Disclaimer: Euronews is owned by Alpac Capital, the same investment firm mentioned in this article as the new owner of N1 television.

Beállítom Magyar Péter és a Tisza Párt tehet arról, hogy Magyarországon 2025-ben csökkent a gyerekszületések száma – jelentette ki Takács Péter fideszes országgyűlési képviselő szombaton, a Digitális Polgári Körök (DPK) első országos táborában tartott beszélgetésen. A YouTube-on élőben közvetített eseményen a Fidesz-kormány egykori egészségügyi államtitkára kijelentette, hogy a romlás 2024 nyarán következett be, és „egyetlen új tényező van 24 nyarán, egyetlen egy, a Tisza Párt és Magyar Péter.” Takács közölte, hogy akkor jól szerepeltek az európai parlamenti választásokon és „csúcsra járatták a mindenszarizmust, hogy te érzed magad rosszul a bőrödben, ez egy élhetetlen ország, egy rossz ország, innen menekülni kell, hülye vagy, ha Magyarországra gyereket szülsz”, és szerinte ezt sulykolta Magyar Péter, és a Tisza Párt tagjai. „Mondhat nekem Magyar Péter bármit, ezt ők okozták, mert elhitették a magyar emberekkel, hogy Magyarország élhetetlen és te egy rossz ember vagy, ha Magyarországra gyereket szülsz” – érvelt Takács. A fideszes politikus előtte a Fidesz családpolitikai támogatásairól beszélt, és közben Kátai-Németh Vilmos szociális és családügyi miniszterről szólva kijelentette, hogy „hú ha, a Kátai, az milyen gonosz ember”, majd hozzátette, hogy „most mondom a nézők kedvéért, hogy nem az a baj vele, hogy vak, hanem, hogy gonosz”. Júliusban Ábrahám Róbert fideszes influenszer, a Pesti Srácok volt munkatársa egy nyilvános rendezvényen vicsorgó vak emberként jellemezte a családügyi minisztert, közölve, hogy „én még olyan rosszindulatú embert nem láttam, de komolyan.” Kátai-Németh Vilmos az első látássérült miniszter a magyar történelemben . Retinasorvadás miatt 16 évesen veszítette el a látását. Később kétdanos aikidómester és thai box edző lett, és látássérült gyerekeknek kezdett harcművészetet tanítani, ő az ország egyetlen vak fekete öves aikidómestere.
